\caption{\textbf{Recovery of clean-code performance under obfuscation.} Every cell is \emph{output prediction}\,/\,\emph{input prediction}; backward is graded by execution. \textbf{The reference is the shaded column}: the untuned model's accuracy on \texttt{L0}, the unobfuscated program. For each arm the first column is its raw accuracy on the condition group and the second is that accuracy \textbf{as a percentage of the shaded reference} --- \textbf{100 means the arm recovers all of the untuned model's clean-code accuracy}, and below 100 means some of it is still lost to the obfuscation. The denominator is the same for every row of a model, so the \texttt{base} column shows how far each condition group degrades the untuned model, and the remaining columns show how much of that each adaptation buys back. \textcolor{green!55!black}{Above} and \textcolor{red!70!black}{below} 100 are coloured; \textbf{bold} marks the best arm in that row and direction. Rows are the condition groups of Appendix~\ref{app:absmaster}: \emph{single} the seen transforms alone, \emph{held-out} the unseen family, \emph{d2--d4} stacks of that depth built only from seen transforms, \emph{d2u}/\emph{d3u} stacks containing the unseen family. The reference is \emph{not} subject to the 0.25 format gate that excludes cells from means --- that gate keeps unreliable measurements out of an average, whereas a denominator is a different object, and untuned format failure reflects adherence to the prompt contract rather than capability (Section~\ref{sec:setup}) --- but a reference whose own rate exceeds the gate carries $\dagger$, so a soft denominator is visible. StarCoder2-15B's untuned forward reading is not merely gated but zero, so it has no forward reference at all. \emph{breadth} and \emph{merge} are exactly data-matched; \emph{router} carries two further experts.}
